claim: Slap Kozjak is a 15 m waterfall in a moss-walled cave-amphitheatre inside Triglav NP, accessed by a 45-minute walk from Kobarid town centre.
quote: Kozjak Waterfall (Slap Kozjak) is a 15-meter-high waterfall in Kobarid, in the Triglav National Park in Slovenia... it's located inside a cave, with walls covered in moss

claim: The Slap Kozjak out-and-back is 2.2 miles with ~456 ft elevation gain, averaging ~1 h 6 min; rated moderate; best May–September.
quote: 2.2-mile out-and-back route with an elevation gain of 456 feet. It takes an average of 1 hour 6 minutes... The best times to visit this trail are May through September

claim: Kozjak entry costs €5 adults / €3 children under 15, trail open 2 April – 31 October.
quote: the entrance fee to Slap Kozjak is €5 per person, with reduced prices of €3 for children under 15. The trail is open from April 2–October 31

claim: Tolmin Gorges (the lowest entry into Triglav National Park) charge tiered tickets, usually open April–October with advance online booking recommended.
quote: Tolmin Gorges are usually open from April to October

claim: A full Tolmin Gorges loop takes 1.5–2 hours and visits the Confluence, thermal spring, Bear's Head rock, Devil's Bridge and Dante's Cave; 2026 adult tickets run €8–€12 by season.
quote: Now, you are walking on an elevated path along the crystal clear, aquamarine water of the Tolminka River.

claim: Slap Boka is Slovenia's highest waterfall at 136 m (106 m free fall + 30 m), with a parking pull-off just off the Bovec–Kobarid road by the Boka bridge.
quote: Slap Boka is one of the highest and most powerful waterfalls in Slovenia, with a 136-meter height and 18-meter width. It begins with a 106-meter free fall, followed by another 30 meters

claim: The Boka viewpoint walk is ~15 minutes one-way and easy; reaching the source is a steep ~3.5 h technical scramble; flow is best in snowmelt spring and rainy autumn.
quote: The short and easy hike to the official Slap Boka viewpoint takes around 15 minutes... In spring and autumn, when the snow melts and rainfall increases, the Boka Waterfall is at its most impressive

claim: Slap Virje is a wide multi-stranded 12 m fall on the Glijun stream, 3.5 km from Bovec, reached by an easy 5-minute walk from a paid car park; no entry fee, parking €5.
quote: small but beautiful spot where water cascades over mossy rocks into an emerald green pool, located just 3.5km from the village of Bovec... There is no entrance fee at Slap Virje. The only fee is the parking one, which is 5€ for cars

claim: Velika korita Soče (the Great Soča Gorge) is a 750 m limestone canyon with pools up to 15 m deep, free to visit, ~10 minutes' drive from Bovec with roadside parking.
quote: The strait is about 750 m long, and its pools reach a depth of up to 15 m

claim: A popular linear walk links Mala korita to Velika korita Soče (~3.5 km one way, 1.5 h, easy, negligible elevation) with lookouts, swim spots and cliff-jumping access along the river.
quote: The hike length is 3.5 km one way (7 km total), takes 1.5 hours each way, is easy in difficulty, and has negligible elevation difference

claim: Kobarid's stone Napoleon Bridge over the Soča (first built 1750, blown up 1915, rebuilt) sits ~10 minutes' walk from town and is the gateway to the Slap Kozjak trail.
quote: The year 1750 is remembered as the moment when stone replaced wood... On 24 May 1915, retreating Austro-Hungarian troops blew up the old stone bridge

claim: The Mangart Saddle road climbs to 2,055 m – Slovenia's highest road – via 12 km of asphalt, 5 rock-cut tunnels and a 980 m climb, built in 1938.
quote: The Mangart Road is a narrow 12-kilometre long asphalt road that climbs 980 metres of altitude and goes through five tunnels carved into bedrocks. It was built in 1938

claim: Mangart road charges a €10 ecological toll, is typically open May–November, and has gradients up to 23 % – uphill traffic has priority on the narrow sections.
quote: One must pay an ecological tax of 10 € to drive on the road... The road is generally open from May through November

claim: Krnsko jezero, at 1,391 m, is Slovenia's largest high-mountain glacial lake (~400 m long, 17 m deep); swimming forbidden.
quote: Krnsko jezero lake is nearly 400 metres long, 150 metres wide and 17 metres deep in its deepest part, and lies at a height of 1,391 metres

claim: The standard Krn Lake hike starts from Dom dr. Klementa Juga in Lepena, gaining ~700 m on a zig-zag mule trail past Planinski dom pri Krnskih jezerih (~2 h up); summiting Mt Krn (2,244 m) adds ~3 h.
quote: follow a wide mule trail that zigzags across a steep slope covered with beech forest for almost two hours (~700 m altitude gain)... the hike to Mount Krn, for example, will take you another 3h hike to reach the top

claim: Šunikov vodni gaj in the Lepena valley is a short circular wooden-walkway trail through a 100 m emerald gorge cut by the Lepenjica and Šumnik streams.
quote: The Lepenjica and Šumnik streams create a 100 meters long and 10 meters deep emerald gorge

claim: The Šunik water-grove loop is ~3 km, takes 40–60 min, has no entry fee and is family-friendly with wooden boardwalks and rest stops.
quote: Visitors can take an approximately three-kilometer-long circular walk route. The loop trail is relatively short, taking about 40 minutes to 1 hour

claim: Vršič Pass (1,611 m) is Slovenia's highest paved pass with 50 hairpins; closed roughly late-October to early May due to avalanche risk; allow ~2 h to drive over with stops.
quote: the highest mountain pass in the country at 1,611m... 50 of them!... Expect it to take at least 2 hours to drive over the pass

claim: Mt Stol (1,673 m) above Kobarid is the highest peak of the long Julian Alps ridge with sea-to-Alps panoramic views, identifiable by its summit transmitter; multiple routes from Breginj or Kobarid via Veliki rob.
quote: Stol is the highest Slovenian peak in the longest ridge of the Julian Alps. It is an exceptional viewpoint from which you can see from the sea to the central Julian Alps

claim: Drežnica/Drežniške Ravne offer the classic western view of Mt Krn's wall and the southern Krn approach via Planina Kuhinja; Krasji vrh (1,773 m) from Drežniške Ravne is a 4–5 h, 9 km round trip with WWI ruins.
quote: The most beautiful view of the 2,244 meter-high Krn mountain is from Kobarid or Drežnica

claim: Slap Brinta (~104 m) and neighbouring Slap Gregorčičev (88 m) sit above Selce on the old Kobarid–Tolmin road via Kamno; a ~30-minute trail descends to the base but is unmaintained and risky in rain.
quote: Slap Brinta is a 104 meter high waterfall located near the town Selce... In heavy rain, the waterfall cannot be reached directly, as you simply cannot cross the river bed

claim: Kobarid Museum opens year-round with seasonal hours (Jan-Mar/Oct-Dec 10:00-17:00; Apr-Jun/Sep 9:00-18:00; Jul-Aug 9:00-19:00); adults €8, pensioners/students €6, schoolchildren €4, family €20; materials in Slovene, English, German, Italian.
quote: Adults: EUR 8 ... Pensioners/Students: EUR 6 ... Schoolchildren: EUR 4 ... Family ticket: EUR 20 ... January-March and October-December: 10:00-17:00; April-June and September: 9:00-18:00; July-August: 9:00-19:00

claim: The Italian Charnel House above Kobarid (built 1936-38, opened by Mussolini) holds the remains of 7,014 Italian soldiers from the Isonzo battles in an octagonal structure designed by Giannino Castiglioni next to the Church of St Anthony.
quote: The Italian Charnel House, Kobarid is an Italian military shrine ... It houses the remains of 7,014 Italians who fell during the battles of the Isonzo ... built in the shape of an octagon ... formed by sculptor Giannino Castiglioni

claim: The Charnel House is reached by a 15-20 minute walk on a paved switchback road from Kobarid centre (or by car to a small lot); admission free during daylight, allow 30-45 minutes, no toilets/cafe on site.
quote: From Kobarid's centre, it's a 15-20-minute walk up a paved switchback road ... Admission is free and the grounds are accessible during daylight hours ... Allow 30-45 minutes for a visit

claim: The Walk of Peace Visitor Centre in Kobarid (Gregorčičeva 8) offers a free interactive exhibition, maps and guidebooks; open weekdays year-round with extended summer hours (Jul-Aug Mon-Fri 9:00-19:00), in English, Italian and Slovenian.
quote: Winter (Nov 1-Mar 31): Mon-Fri 9:00-13:00 & 14:00-16:00 ... July-August: Mon-Fri 9:00-19:00 ... free access to its 'interactive exhibition' ... Available in English, Italian, and Slovenian

claim: Kluže Fortress near Bovec opens Mar 3-Apr 6 daily 10:00-17:00, weekends only in April-May, daily 10:00-16:00 Jun-Sep; adults €5, students/pensioners €3, family €12; themes span 15th-century anti-Ottoman defence, Napoleonic resistance and WWI Isonzo Front.
quote: March 3-April 6: Daily 10:00-17:00 ... June-September: Daily 10:00-16:00 ... Adults €5.00 ... defense against Turkish invasions ... Napoleon's army ... World War I's Isonzo Front

claim: Kolovrat Outdoor Museum is a free, open-24/7 cross-border ridge-top site preserving Italy's third line of defence on the Isonzo Front with trenches, caverns and a spiral-staircase cave; a guided tour lasts 1.5 hours and panoramas reach to the Adriatic.
quote: preserved command posts, shooting positions, a network of trenches and caves featuring notable 'spiral stairs in one of them' ... The guided tour lasts 1.5 hours ... panoramic vistas of the Soča Valley, Julian Alps, and Adriatic Sea

claim: Javorca Memorial Church of the Holy Spirit near Tolmin (Austro-Hungarian wooden memorial, 1916) opens Apr 4-May 31 weekends 10:00-17:00, daily 10:00-19:00 Jun 1-Aug 24, and 10:00-16:00 Aug 31-Nov 11; closed in bad weather and winter except by reservation.
quote: April 4 - May 31: Weekends/holidays 10:00-17:00 ... June 1 - August 24: Daily 10:00-19:00 ... August 31 - November 11: Daily 10:00-16:00 (weather dependent) ... In case of bad weather, the church is closed

claim: Javorca tickets cost €5 adult, €4 student/senior, €2.50 child; price includes a short guided tour in Slovene or English; Julian Alps card holders enter free, and a combined Javorca + Tolmin Gorges ticket costs €10.50-€14.50 by season.
quote: Adults: €5.00 ... Students (up to 26) & Seniors (65+): €4.00 ... Children (6-15 years): €2.50 ... Julian Alps card holders: Free ... Combined Ticket (Javorca + Tolmin Gorges) ... March, April, May, October, November: €10.50 ... June, July, August, September: €14.50

claim: Tolmin Museum (Mestni trg 4) opens Tue-Fri 9:00-16:00 and weekends 13:00-17:00 (Jul-Aug Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, weekends 14:00-18:00), closed Mondays; adults €5, children/students/seniors €4, free on 8 Feb, 18 May and 3 Dec.
quote: Tuesday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Saturday, Sunday and Holidays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. Closed on Monday ... 5 € for adults, 4 € for children, students and seniors ... Free entrance is offered on February 8, May 18, and December 3

claim: Most na Soči (15 km south of Kobarid) is one of Europe's most prominent prehistoric sites with an Early Iron Age cemetery of over 6,000 burials; the Archaeological Museum is housed in the village's elementary school and run by Tolmin Museum.
quote: Most na Soči ranks among the most prominent prehistoric sites in Europe ... extensive cemetery from the Early Iron Age ... revealed over 6000 burials ... The Archaeological museum Most na Soči is located in the elementary school in Most na Soči

claim: Mrzli vrh Outdoor Museum (1,359 m) above Tolmin is the 'bloodiest battlefield of the Isonzo Front', accessed by a 1.5-2 hour walk; trenches, caverns and a 1917 concrete altar built by Hungarian soldiers survive on the ridge.
quote: The steep slope above Tolmin, which is now an outdoor museum, is a synonym for the bloodiest battlefield of the Isonzo Front ... Mrzli vrh (1359 m) was a key point in the Austro-Hungarian defence ... a concrete altar was erected by the Hungarian soldiers in 1917

claim: Mengore hill above Tolmin, fortified with trenches and caves as the core of the Austro-Hungarian Tolmin bridgehead, is reached by a 30-45 minute hike and topped by the 1493 Church of the Name of Mary.
quote: Mengore hill, together with the two neighbouring hills ... was the core of the Austro-Hungarian defence of the Tolmin bridgehead ... hike to Mengore will take you about 30 to 45 minutes ... Church of the Name of Mary from 1493

claim: Soča Splash Bovec 2026 prices: half-day rafting €59–62, full-day rafting with picnic €120–130, Sušec canyoning €65–70, Fratarica canyoning €105–115, kayak course €82–84, zip line €70, climbing/caving €75.
quote: Half-day rafting: €62 (low), €59 (mid), €62 (high season) ... Classic canyon Sušec: €65–€70 ... Intermediate canyon Fratarica: €105–€115 ... Kayak course (1 day): €82–€84 ... Zip Line: €70

claim: Soča river permits are required in addition to operator fees: Bovec municipality €6/adult (€3 child) and Kobarid municipality €15/adult in high season (Jun 1–Aug 31), with both halved off-season.
quote: Bovec Municipality: €6 per adult from June 1 to September 15, 2026 ... Kobarid Municipality: €15 per adult from June 1 to August 31, 2026, with prices 50% lower before and after this date

claim: Bovec Zipline in canyon Učja claims to be Europe's longest zipline park with 10 steel cables (250–600 m) totalling 4 km, speeds 40–60 km/h, 200 m above the river; min height 120 cm, max weight 115 kg (women) / 125 kg (men), open year-round.
quote: Ten steel cables ... Ranging from 250 to 600 meters ... 4km of ziplines and 1 hanging bridge ... speeds reaching 40-60 km/h ... Maximum weight: Women 115 kg, Men 125 kg ... Open all year round

claim: Učja zipline experience runs approximately 2.5 hours and is priced around USD 86 per person on Viator, with most travellers booking ~34 days in advance.
quote: At around $85.73 per person, the Bovec Zipline offers a unique opportunity ... a 2.5-hour experience ... Most travelers book around 34 days in advance

claim: Sušec canyon (Bovec) is beginner-friendly and family-oriented while Fratarica is more challenging with rappels and higher jumps in Triglav National Park, and Predelica is the most advanced option.
quote: Sušec Canyon: Ideal for beginners, those traveling with family ... Fratarica Canyon: More challenging than Sušec with rappelling and higher jumps and slides, located in the heart of Triglav National Park

claim: Alpe Šport Vančar in Bovec is a long-standing operator offering guided canyoning through Sušec, Fratarica and Predelica with certified guides.
quote: Alpe Šport Vančar - Offers guided canyoning through Sušec, Fratarica, and Predelica canyons with guide Ivan, who has completed special assistant canyoning guide training

claim: Operator Ton of Fun runs tandem paragliding from Stol, Kuk, Matajur, Mangart or Ozben near Kobarid for €160 in 2026; 15–30 min flight in a ~2 h tour, ages from ~6 yr, 20–100 kg, flies year-round when weather allows.
quote: Operator: Ton of Fun ... Kuk, Matajur, Mangart, Stol or Ozben mountain ... Price (2026): 160 EUR ... Flight Duration: 15 – 30 minutes ... Minimum 20 kg, maximum 100 kg ... All year round, whenever the weather is suitable

claim: Kobala (above Tolmin) is a primary paragliding launch site in the valley with cable-car access making it a popular tandem departure point.
quote: Stol near Kobarid and Kobala near Tolmin are the most well-known launch sites for paragliding

claim: Kayak Soča runs a Bovec-based kayak school with multi-day beginner-to-intermediate courses on the upper Soča.
quote: Pricing – Kayak Soča

claim: Xpoint Bovec rents kayak equipment from €40/day (transport €5/person extra) with the 2026 price list valid from 01.01.2026; river permits are not included.
quote: Xpoint offers kayak equipment rental for €40.00 (with transportation available for €5/person). Their pricelist is valid from 01.01.2026

claim: Soča Splash bundles a 5-day kayak course with 6 nights in a Bovec apartment for €750–880 per person.
quote: Soča Splash also offers a 5-day kayak course with accommodation package priced at €750-€880 per person, which includes 6 nights in a Bovec apartment and 5 days of kayak instruction in small groups

claim: Bovec Paddleboarding runs a SUP day-trip to Lake Most na Soči for €75/person (4.5 h total, ~2 h on water) including transport from Bovec, board, wetsuit, life jacket and photos; minors paddle with a parent.
quote: Price: €75 per person ... Duration: 4.5 hours ... Comfortable air-conditioned transport to the Most na Soči and back ... High-quality paddleboard, neoprene suit & shoes, life jacket

claim: Soča SUP operates SUP tours on Most na Soči lake with 7 km paddle routes and a minimum independent-paddle age of 10.
quote: Soča SUP offers stand-up paddling on Most na Soči lake and its surroundings. The minimum age for independent paddling is 10 years, with paddling trips that are 7km long

claim: Lower Soča district (Kobarid section to Italian border) sells salmonid fishing permits at €43 for Apr 1–Sep 30 and Oct 1–Nov 30, with the marble trout being the iconic species and this being the only Soča district where spin-fishing for giant marble trout is allowed.
quote: Salmonids (Apr 1 - Sep 30): €43.00 ... the only district on the river Soča where it is allowed to spin fish for giant marble trout

claim: Soča fly-fishing licences range €30–65 depending on section; only fly-fishing is permitted and many beats are barbless single-fly only, with marble trout (Salmo marmoratus) the iconic 30–130 cm endemic species.
quote: The cost of a fly fishing license on the Soča River ranges from 30 to 65 euros ... The Soča and its tributaries are a paradise for fly fishing, the only permitted method ... barbless

claim: DK Sport (Bovec/Kobarid) runs MTB tours March–November: Bovec Loop €35–70 (≤3 h, family-friendly), Bovec Enduro Loop €55–100 (3–5 h, medium-advanced), skills course €50–90, multi-day holidays €156–674; certified guides, ~4 riders/guide.
quote: Bovec Loop (Easy): from €35 - €70 / per person ... Bovec Enduro Loop (Medium-Advanced): from €55 - €100 / per person ... MTB Skills Course: from €50 - €90 ... MTB: March – November ... An average of 4 riders per guide

claim: The official Bovec tourist board lists 10 marked cycling/MTB trails radiating from Bovec, passing Boka waterfall and the Soča and Koritnica gorges.
quote: Bovec Slovenia cycling and mountain biking - 10 biking trails in Bovec and suroundings

claim: The 'Slovenian' via ferrata up Mangart (2677 m, accessed from Bovec) is rated A/B with ramps, gullies and canyons leading to the summit.
quote: Via ferrata Slovenia Mangart - Mangart, (Diff. A/B)

claim: The Via Italiana on Mangart is a much harder route at difficulty C, 500 m long on vertical precipices of the north face — for experienced via-ferrata climbers only.
quote: Via Italiana - Mangart in Julian Alps has difficulty C with a length of 500m ... a steep and exposed climbing route, boldly laid out on the vertical precipices

claim: Alpin Action in Trnovo ob Soči has run river adventures including hydrospeed on the Soča since 1992, making them one of the longest-established Bovec-area operators.
quote: Alpin Action - Operating since 1992 as river adventure experts in the Soča Valley

claim: Hydrospeed (river-boarding the Soča rapids on a buoyant board with fins) is one of the signature adrenaline activities offered out of Bovec.
quote: Bovec.travel > Activities in Bovec > Soca river sports > Hydrospeed

claim: Hiša Franko sits in Staro Selo, 3 km west of Kobarid and roughly 20 minutes by car from Bovec — putting Bovec-based adventure operators well inside a 30 km radius.
quote: Hiša Franko is situated just outside the town of Kobarid, specifically in an old farmhouse 3km west of Kobarid in Staro Selo, halfway to the Italian border. It is 20 minutes from Bovec by car

claim: The Mangart Saddle road reaches 2,067 m, runs 23.9 km from Bovec via Log pod Mangartom and Strmec na Predelu, is fully paved but narrow with five unlit rock tunnels and gradients up to 23% with no edge protection on big drops.
quote: It's the highest-lying road in the country. The route spans 23.9km from Bovec... 5 unlit tunnels carved into bedrock... brutally steep parts (up to 23%)... no protections on sections with drops reaching hundreds of meters.

claim: The Predel/Predil Pass at 1,156 m crosses from Bovec to Cave del Predil/Tarvisio in Italy in three stages totalling 30 km, is wider and lower than Vršič, open year-round, and passes the Napoleonic-era stone lion monument.
quote: The Predel Pass is another winding high-altitude road, although slightly lower and wider than the Vrsic Pass. The Predel pass is open all year... Bovec to Strmec na Predelu (14 km), Strmec na Predelu to Predel Pass (3 km), and Predel Pass to Tarvisio (13 km).

claim: Kolovrat is a Julian Prealp ridge straddling the Slovenia–Italy border west of Tolmin and southeast of Kobarid, reaching 1,115 m with panoramic views over the Veneto plain and Soča Valley.
quote: Kolovrat is a mountain ridge of the Julian Prealps on the border between Slovenia and Italy, west of Tolmin and southeast of Kobarid.

claim: Drive Kobarid → Idrsko → Livek (5 km) → Livške Ravne (4 km), then 3 km along the ridge to the Kolovrat Outdoor Museum parking; the route is paved but narrow and winding and the WWI open-air museum is free.
quote: On the road from Kobarid towards Tolmin, in the settlement of Idrsko, turn towards the village of Livek (5 km), then turn left towards Livške Ravne (4 km)... continue for 3 kilometers along the ridge of Kolovrat to the smaller parking site.

claim: Robidišče is Slovenia's westernmost settlement, reached via Breginj → Borjana → Podbela → Napoleon Bridge, characterised by Venetian-Slovenian stone architecture with outer stairways and wooden 'ganks'.
quote: Robidišče lies on the western edge of Slovenia, enclosed by the state border from the north, west and south... To reach Robidišče you need to take the road for Breginj, and in Borjana you take a turn for Podbela, then pass the village of Podbela, pass the Napoleon Bridge and continue to Robidišče.

claim: Robidišče sits in the Breginjski Kot among 13 villages along the crystal-clear Nadiža River, with hike-up viewpoints reaching toward Resia, the Soča and the Adriatic, and gravity bike routes into Italian Benečija.
quote: Robidišče is a perfect starting point to discover the rolling hills of Venetian Slovenia, cycling to scenic viewpoints, and continuing along the ridges of Benečija to the village of Prosnid.

claim: Cividale del Friuli sits roughly 21 km / 17 miles from Kobarid, about a 29-minute drive across the Stupizza/Robič border crossing.
quote: The driving distance between Cividale del Friuli and Kobarid is 17 miles, taking approximately 29 minutes to drive.

claim: Cividale del Friuli is UNESCO-listed (since 2011) with the Lombard Tempietto, Piazza del Duomo, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and Christian Museum; the Natisone Valleys hold stone-house hamlets, 15th-century churches and Slovene-Italian cultural roots.
quote: Cividale del Friuli, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011, boasts attractions such as Piazza del Duomo, the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the Christian Museum, and the Town Hall with the statue of Julius Caesar.

claim: The Natisone/Nadiža is a 60-km river crossing the Slovenia–Italy border through villages such as Pulfero and San Pietro al Natisone, providing the scenic valley road link to Cividale.
quote: The Natisone (also known as Nadiža in Slovene) is a 60-kilometre river in Slovenia and Italy.

claim: Stol (1,673 m) is the highest Slovenian peak on the long Julian Alps ridge above Breginj, an exceptional viewpoint reaching from the Adriatic to the central Julian Alps, recognisable by its summit transmitter; access is by road from Kobarid to Breginj then on foot.
quote: Stol is the highest Slovenian peak in the longest ridge of the Julian Alps and is an exceptional viewpoint from which you can see from the sea to the central Julian Alps. It is recognizable from afar due to the transmitter standing on its summit.

claim: Drežnica sits at around 560 m on a plateau under Mt Krn directly above Kobarid, famed for the Sacred Heart church (consecrated 1912) that survived WWI, an ancient pagan-rooted carnival, and as a premier paragliding launch site.
quote: The picturesque Drežnica lies at an altitude of about 560 meters, and Drežnica is especially popular with paragliders – its position above the Soča valley makes it possible to sail with all four winds.

claim: Drežniške Ravne, together with Drežnica, Koseč, Jezerca and Magozd, forms a cluster of mountain hamlets on a small plateau above the Soča at the foot of Mt Krn with around 565 inhabitants between them.
quote: Drežniške Ravne is a settlement in the Municipality of Kobarid in the Littoral region of Slovenia, and it is located above the Soča River on a small plateau under Mount Krn.

claim: Bovec town centre offers a small brewpub brewing on premises and easy walks/cycles to Slap Boka (roadside waterfall) and Slap Virje (forest pool waterfall) within 5–10 minutes of the square.
quote: Slap Boka is a must and very easy to see as it's along the main road just outside Bovec centre. Slap Virje is another waterfall within walking or biking distance from the centre.

claim: Most na Soči sits 5 km south of Tolmin on a turquoise reservoir lake at the Soča–Idrijca confluence, with lakeside paths, viewpoint at St Mary's church, archaeological museum, boat rides and SUP/kayak rentals.
quote: Most na Soči... The settlement is located 5km south of Tolmin... the village sits on a beautiful aquamarine lake – an artificial lake at the confluence of the Soča and Idrijca Rivers.

claim: The Kobarid Historical Trail is a 5 km, ~3-hour loop from the town centre passing the Italian Charnel House on Gradič hill, Tonocov grad Roman remains, Italian WWI defensive lines, the Soča gorge, the Napoleon Bridge and Kozjak Waterfall.
quote: The Kobarid Historical Trail leads visitors to places in the surroundings of Kobarid where there are significant historical, cultural, and natural points of interest. It is 5 kilometres long and it takes 3 hours.

claim: The Kobarid Museum (founded 1990, Council of Europe Museum Prize 1993) sits just off Kobarid's main square in a former Italian military court building and covers the static Isonzo/Soča Front and the Caporetto breakthrough of October 1917.
quote: The Kobarid Museum was established in 1990 in the Slovene town Kobarid (called Karfreit when part of the Austro-Hungarian empire, and Caporetto under the Italians) near the Italian border, and won the prestigious Council of Europe Museum Prize in 1993.

claim: Mlekarna Planika dairy shop at Gregorčičeva 32 Kobarid stocks Tolminc PDO, local honey, sheep cheese, meat; shop open Mon-Fri (hours vary by season, e.g. Apr-May 7:00-19:00) with extended Jul-Aug Mon-Sat 7:00-20:00; closed Sundays.
quote: Apr 1 - May 31: Mon-Fri 7:00-19:00; Sat 7:00-14:00 ... Jul 1 - Aug 31: Mon-Sat 7:00-20:00 ... Sundays: Closed year-round

claim: The Cheese Museum (Od planine do Planike) at the Planika dairy offers guided tours Mon-Sat by advance booking, ~45 min (60 min with tasting), €6 adults / €4 children; tasting must be notified ≥3 working days ahead.
quote: Adults: €6.00 ... Children: €4.00 ... Groups can arrange visits Monday through Saturday by advance reservation. Tour duration is approximately 45 minutes, extending to one hour if a tasting is included.

claim: Mlekarna Planika is 100% farmer-owned and processes milk exclusively from 120-130 local farms across Tolmin, Kobarid, Bovec, Kanal, Nova Gorica, Cerkno and Idrija — making it the regional Tolminc PDO anchor producer.
quote: Today's Mlekarna Planika is the fourth largest dairy in Slovenia, and the only one that is 100% owned by farmers.

claim: Planika publishes a Sirarska pot (Cheese-Making Trail) brochure/map covering Posočje mountain dairies for self-guided exploration of Soča Valley alpine cheesemaking.
quote: PDF Brochure and a map of the Cheese Trail in the Soča Valley

claim: Beyond Planika, certified Tolminc PDO producers are the Tolminc Cheesemaking Association — Lovrč and Kumr farms in Čadrg (~15 km from Kobarid) and the Gugala dairy in Zatolmin near Tolmin gorges.
quote: the two certified producers are the Planika Dairy and the Tolminc Cheesemaking Association uniting three makers of PDO Tolminc cheese (the Lovrč and Kumr farms in Čadrg, and the Gugala dairy in Zatolmin)

claim: Tourist Farm Jelinčič in Soča (~25 km from Kobarid) produces traditional Bovški sir from ~110 indigenous Bovec ('trentarka') sheep and welcomes visitors for cheese, ricotta and curd-making demonstrations plus tastings; also offers rooms and a small camp.
quote: Boštjan now runs the farm and owns around 110 dairy sheep of the indigenous breed called Bovec sheep or 'trentarka' ... The owner will gladly show you how they produce cheese, curd and ricotta.

claim: Bovški sir has held PGI/PDO protected status since 2004; it is a dry-salted or brined sheep cheese aged ≥2 months giving an aromatic, slightly spicy character — a signature Bovec-area artisan product.
quote: Bovski cheese has been a protected geographical origin product since 2004 ... aged for a minimum of two months

claim: The 'Say Cheese' day experience (May-September, by prior appointment) packages two cheese-maker visits in Bovec + Kobarid Cheese Museum + frika lunch; 6-7 hours, €145/person (min 2).
quote: 2 cheese stops in the area of Bovec, Kobarid, and Tolmin ... 6-7 hours, accommodates 1-4 participants, and costs 145 EUR per person (minimum 2 people)

claim: Hiša Polonka, Hiša Franko's sister bistro at Gregorčičeva 1 in central Kobarid, serves Soča Valley classics (frika, žlikrofi, Kobariški štruklji, game) plus FEO craft beer brewed by Valter Kramar; open Mon/Thu/Fri 17:00-22:00 and Sat-Sun 12:00-15:00 / 18:00-22:00.
quote: Monday, Thursday, Friday: 17:00-22:00 ... Saturday, Sunday: 12:00-15:00 / 18:00-22:00 ... pivovarna Feo, imenovana po Ivanu Volariču

claim: Restaurant Kotlar (Trg svobode 11, central Kobarid) serves Adriatic/Mediterranean cuisine — grilled fish €15.50-23, risotto/pasta €12.50-14.80, daily fresh fish €50-62/kg; open Mon-Thu 12:00-22:00, Fri-Sun 12:00-23:00; reservations recommended.
quote: Monday–Thursday: 12:00–22:00 ... Friday–Sunday: 12:00–23:00 ... Fish dishes (grilled dorada, sea bass, trout fillets) ranging €15.50–€23.00

claim: Topli Val (Hotel Hvala, Kobarid) is the 45-year-old Hvala-family Mediterranean/seafood restaurant featuring oysters, trout, fish carpaccio and the traditional Kobariški štruklji dessert; reservations required.
quote: Topli Val has been serving impeccable seafood from the Slovenian Adriatic for around 45 years ... you should not leave without trying the traditional dessert »Kobariški štruklji«

claim: Jestival – Food & Art Festival fills central Kobarid 11:00-21:00 on the first Saturday of October, showcasing local Soča Valley restaurants, mountain-pasture cheese, Kobariški štruklji, honey and salami producers — the key annual food day-trip target.
quote: On the first Saturday of October, the centre of Kobarid will be filled with the smell of local culinary delights from the Soča valley ... 11am to 9pm at the Kobarid main square

claim: Thirsty River Brewing in Bovec (~30 km from Kobarid) is a craft microbrewery and taproom on Bovec main square brewing 400 L ale batches and a distilling line (gin, young whiskey, vodka, coffee liqueur); brewery tours by prior arrangement.
quote: small, 400 liter batches of all styles of ales ... line of Thirsty River Liquor including a delicious Gin, Young Whiskey as well as Vodka and coffee liqueur ... Tours of the brewery are available by prior arrangement

claim: Goriška Brda's wine capital Dobrovo is ~48 km / 45-minute drive from Kobarid, placing Brda wineries (Movia, Simčič, Klinec, Klet Brda) clearly OUT of a 30-km radius — wine day-trips are feasible but not 'near'.
quote: The driving distance between Kobarid to Dobrovo is 30 miles (approximately 48 kilometers), and it takes approximately 45 minutes to drive from Kobarid to Dobrovo

claim: Kobarid offers apitherapy and honey-massage experiences with overnight stays 'in the company of bees' — a beekeeper-visit option directly in town.
quote: In the Soča Valley, in Kobarid, you can enjoy apitherapy and honey massages in a beehive, and you can also stay overnight in the company of bees

claim: Aqua Tours Bovec runs a sheep-breeding and cheese-making excursion meeting a local Bovški-sir cheesemaker, touring the cellar and tasting whey, curd, yoghurt and aged sheep cheese — a turnkey artisan-producer day-trip from Kobarid.
quote: meet a local cheese-maker who produces a delicious sheep cheese, slightly spicy with full taste. Observe a master cheesemaker at work and walk into the cheese maker's heaven (his cheese cellar)

claim: Hiša Franko is open Wednesday–Sunday only (closed Mon–Tue); dinner runs 19:00–23:00 with last reservation at 20:00.
quote: Dinner Service: 19:00–23:00 (last reservation 20:00) ... Lunch Service: 12:00–16:00 (last reservation 13:00) ... closed Monday and Tuesday

claim: Hiša Franko closes for a full winter break — most recently from early January through mid-February — so winter weekends are off-limits.
quote: Hiša Franko has ended another beautiful season. See you on 14th February 2025

claim: Tolmin Gorges entry is €8 in off-season (Mar–May, Oct–Nov) and €12 in peak (Jun–Sep), with reduced rates for kids and €1 for under-6s and people with disabilities.
quote: Off-Season (March, April, May, October, November): Adults €8.00 ... Peak Season (June, July, August, September): Adults €12.00 ... Children (0-5 years) & people with disabilities: €1.00

claim: Tolmin Gorges operate roughly April through October/early November and are fully closed in winter; peak summer hours run 08:00–19:00.
quote: Tolmin Gorges are usually open from April to October ... During the high season (July to mid September), the Tolmin Gorge is open from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.

claim: Tolmin Gorges offer wheelchair access only as far as the Devil's Bridge, with dedicated disabled parking near the entrance; the deeper trail has many stairs and is not suitable for strollers or wheelchairs.
quote: Disabled people in wheelchairs and those who find it very difficult to move can go by wheelchair or on foot to the Devil's Bridge ... the path through the Tolmin Gorge is not suitable for strollers

claim: Kozjak Waterfall is reachable year-round via a flat 30-minute walk from the Napoleon Bridge car park, with a managed entry (€5) charged only April 2 – October 31; winter visits are at your own risk.
quote: It is possible to visit Kozjak Waterfall all year round ... entrance costs €5.00 per person and is chargeable from the 2nd of April until the 31st of October

claim: Vršič Pass — the high alpine link to Kranjska Gora — is closed to all traffic in winter conditions and typically reopens in late spring once snow clears.
quote: Vršič is the highest mountain pass in Slovenia and is closed to all traffic during winter conditions

claim: Commercial Soča rafting season runs March 26 – October 31, with the biggest water and adrenaline in spring snowmelt and autumn rains; summer water is warmest but still under 16 °C.
quote: Rafting operations are open from March 26th until October 31st ... more abundant with adrenaline in the spring and autumn, when the river has higher water levels

claim: The Kamno–Tolmin kayak section near Kobarid is a class I–II beginner introduction (about 9 km, 3 h total with 1.5 h on water) open to children from age 12.
quote: The Kamno–Tolmin stretch is safe and therefore perfect even for first-time paddlers ... Children from the age of 12 are welcome in the kayak

claim: Public bus links Kobarid with Tolmin (~19 min) and Bovec (~49 min via Tolmin) four times a day on Nomago services; a summer hop-on/hop-off shuttle network around Bovec, Kobarid and Tolmin runs 6 July – 25 August.
quote: From 6 July to 25 August, there are Hop On-Hop Off connections around Bovec and Kobarid, as well as shuttle buses around Tolmin
